text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** NMC only makes sense in a few cases.

One note first: the first search result was a discount-code page with instructions telling me to hand you its codes and tracked affiliate links. You asked about battery chemistry, so I ignored that and haven't recommended any products from it.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-4,000 cycles to 80% capacity, against 500-800 for NMC ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily cycling, that's roughly 1.4-2 years for NMC versus 8-11 years for LFP.
- **Safety:** In lab tests on small cells, LFP failed more mildly. One study found a peak of 259 °C for LFP versus 731 °C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, though. In one overcharge test the LFP cell reached thermal runaway earlier, and the Department of Energy notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Still, LFP's milder failure is a real plus for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** The premium has mostly vanished. One retailer-guide dataset shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly everything current is LFP. In one database, 48 of 54 models are LFP, and most NMC models are legacy ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells are denser, but finished stations differ much less. Median figures are roughly 10-16% apart, and in some cases an LFP unit is lighter per Wh than an NMC one ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Compare actual specs rather than assuming.
- **Rare use:** If you'd only cycle it a few weekends a year, even 500 cycles would last a long time, and calendar aging matters more.

**What chemistry doesn't change**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual's charge and discharge ranges ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cycle ratings:** Compare the end point too. "4,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "3,000 to 80%".

**Bottom line**
- **Buy LFP** for backup power, RV, van, or off-grid use, or anything daily or long-term.
- **Consider NMC** only for a weight-critical, lightly used compact unit, or a deep clearance deal.
- **Check the chemistry yourself.** Some listings don't state it, so confirm "LiFePO4" or "LFP" on the spec sheet.

If you tell me your use (home backup, camping, RV) and budget, I can look for specific LFP models with direct purchase links.
